summary: Bounded Safetensors headers, exact tensor roles and packed-shard geometry
implementation_scope: Metadata inspection through Core's strict safetensors reader (crit_core.model) under the audit policy, and engine-supplied role/capability/packed-geometry audits; no tensor payload decoding or inference

agent_guidance.use_when: Check that an imported artifact contains the exact tensor roles and local codec geometry required by an engine
agent_guidance.avoid_when: A qualified importer already enforces these checks, or unsupported container/dtype/layout semantics are needed
provides: Audit policy over Core's strict reader: strict flat indexes, no symbolic links, tighter limits and byte-addressable dtypes only
Actual header shape/storage-dtype matching against exact required tensor roles
Requested-capability metadata status separate from observed proposer invocation
Packed local K-word/group-scale geometry and namespace checks
engine_supplies: Immutable trusted source snapshot, complete required roles and architecture/config/tokenizer interpretation
Exact codec value semantics, numerical validation, tensor loading and payload content identity
Qualified synchronous proposer, target verification, mutable-state repair and publication
Physical allocations, stream completion and source retention when loading audited regions
preserve: Read actual tensor headers rather than trusting names, counts or descriptive dtype claims
Reject inconsistent shard maps, unsupported representations and incomplete requested roles
Keep local packed words and scales aligned to the same K slice and declared matrix namespace
Metadata readiness never establishes runtime arithmetic, model quality or performance
adapt: Bounded container/dtype support and engine-supplied architecture schemas
Additional explicit codec geometry, tensor naming and runtime observation hooks

code_files.purpose: Checked metadata reader, exact role/capability audit, packed K-shard geometry and separate proposer probe
Runnable tiny synthetic artifact, required MTP roles, local packed-scale audit and observed toy proposer invocation

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ with crit_core (Core's Python package, standard library only); no GPU or model download
requires.model: Supported byte-addressable Safetensors headers and exact engine-supplied tensor-role/codec schemas
requires.workload: Read-only import preflight on a bounded immutable source snapshot; no tensor arithmetic

contract.input: One .safetensors file or strict flat .safetensors.index.json plus ModelSchema with exact required roles
contract.output: Immutable ModelInventory metadata and AuditResult bindings/capability_status, with an optional separate ProposerProbe
contract.ownership: Metadata file descriptors close after inspection. The engine freezes source bytes, rechecks identity before loading and retains actual allocations through completion.
contract.failure: Reject duplicate/malformed JSON, invalid extents, holes/overlap/truncation, index escapes/contradictions, missing roles and inconsistent packed shard geometry. I/O and probe hook failures propagate.
contract.core_boundary: Container parsing is Core's strict safetensors reader (crit_core.model inspect_safetensors/inspect_model; natively crit::core::Checkpoint); the audit adds its policy and keeps architecture roles and encoding interpretation outside Core. Audited metadata is not an allocation, readiness or model-correctness receipt.

validation.host: Adversarial synthetic header/index/schema fixtures and the runnable example cover actual dtype/shape checks, requested proposer invocation and local K-scale geometry
validation.native: No native parser, GGUF, sub-byte dtype support, FP8 numerical decoding, learned MTP head or model execution is supplied or qualified
validation.performance: Header work is bounded; model import/inference speed and trained-model quality are unmeasured
